title: Canonical shipped distribution subject inventory
description: Objective: establish one production-owned canonical distribution inventory for the exact shipped subject and make the release subject consume it, closing the current five-vs-six component split before cross-host receipts bind a distribution digest. Deliverable: a focused tools/packaging inventory module shared by scripts/release/release-subject.mjs and the distribution integration suite; it includes the landed JetBrains IDE adapter and every exact asset without duplicating a second hand-written inventory. NOT in scope: cross-host receipt generation, publishing evidence, changing distribution signature/manifest semantics, or adding components that are not shipped. Current gap at HEAD 26ac640/8d9afb8: RELEASE_COMPONENTS in scripts/release/release-subject.mjs has five entries and omits the JetBrains adapter, while tests/integration/distribution/distribution-packaging.test.ts independently asserts six. Consumer: task-01c5f96ec1e247dc846fd628c929974a. Owned paths: tools/packaging/distribution-inventory.ts, scripts/release/release-subject.mjs, tests/integration/distribution/distribution-packaging.test.ts. Verification: pnpm typecheck:packaging && pnpm test:integration.
definitionOfDone: One frozen production inventory names exactly the six shipped components, including ide-adapter-jetbrains and its exact real asset set, with no duplicate inventory authority in the release script or integration test.
buildReleaseSubject consumes that inventory and its accepted subject binds all six component manifests/container digests to the same exact source SHA and distribution contract.

Omission, duplication, asset drift, or a caller-supplied alternative inventory fails closed through the existing stable release/distribution refusal code and owning layer; tests assert the exact reason and layer.
The canonical inventory and release subject load under plain Node 24, and task-01c5f96ec1e247dc846fd628c929974a is recorded as the real evidence consumer.
Fresh pnpm typecheck:packaging && pnpm test:integration exits 0.
taskRails: Do not copy the six-entry list into another test helper; both production release and tests consume the one canonical inventory.
Preserve distribution signature, parser, verifier, compatibility, and source-binding authority; this task changes only subject inventory composition.
Use TDD, keep the new production module below 250 lines, and stage only the three explicit owned paths.

FOUR DEVIATIONS FROM THE PLAN:

D-1 (MATERIAL, changes step 2/3/6 literals). The jetbrains asset set is TWELVE paths, not ten. Plan says ":83-92, ten paths"; actual is :80-93 and the test's own assertion at :253 is `expect(shipped[0]!.assets.length).toBe(12)`. Six .js/.ts pairs: ide-contract/src/index, jetbrains-host-port-detail, jetbrains-host-ports, jetbrains-host, jetbrains/src/index, jetbrains-distribution-gate. All 12 verified present on disk with nonzero bytes (28..9568 B). The canonical inventory carries 12 and the literals I pin are 12.

D-2 (NAMING). The guard the plan calls `readComponents` is actually `selectedComponents` at :95-100; the byte comparison `JSON.stringify(value) === JSON.stringify(RELEASE_COMPONENTS)` is at :99. Semantics exactly as the plan describes. `readOwned` is :102-111 (plan said :102-103) and does split("/") + resolve as described, so forward-slash logical paths are required.

D-3 (NEW FINDING, NOT IN THE PLAN — a SECOND divergence the task description does not mention). The split is not only five-vs-six components; provider-claude's ASSET SET also diverges between the two inventories. release-subject.mjs hand-writes ELEVEN claude assets (:33-38). The test does NOT hand-write them — `providerAssets("claude")` (:55-61) is a DIRECTORY WALK, and on disk it yields TWENTY-TWO. The 11 extras are claude-launch-selection, claude-launch-verify, claude-launcher, claude-launcher-authority, claude-launcher-authority-test-fixtures, claude-launcher-boundary-results, claude-launcher-contract, claude-launcher-input, claude-launcher-lifecycle, claude-launcher-port-results, claude-launcher-test-fixtures. Codex matches exactly at 8/8.

D-3 RESOLUTION, and I am flagging it for QA rather than deciding silently: the canonical inventory takes PRODUCTION's eleven-asset claude list, not the walk's twenty-two. Three reasons. (a) release-subject.mjs is the production release authority — it is what actually builds the shipped subject; the test's walk is precisely the duplicate authority DoD 1 orders removed, so unifying onto the walk would promote a test-local list over production. (b) The walk's filter is `.endsWith(".ts") && !.endsWith(".test.ts")`, which does NOT exclude `*-test-fixtures.ts` — it sweeps claude-launcher-test-fixtures.ts and claude-launcher-authority-test-fixtures.ts into a SHIPPED distribution. The test's own comment at :249-252 calls that "the guard against a fixture creeping back in as a shipped artifact, which task rail 2 forbids"; its walk violates the thing it documents. (c) Changing an existing component's asset set changes that component's container digest — explicitly out of scope ("NOT in scope: changing distribution signature/manifest semantics"), and deciding which nine launcher production modules ship is authority this task was not given. Whether those nine belong in the shipped subject is a real open question and wants its own task.

D-4 (SCOPE, already anticipated by the plan). typecheck:release (package.json:26) also compiles release-subject.mjs with --allowJs --checkJs --allowImportingTsExtensions, so it will pull the new module in transitively. That does NOT remove the need for step 5: the DoD's named command is typecheck:packaging, which has neither flag and would still compile only two files. Step 5 stands. Note for step 3: because typecheck:packaging lacks --allowImportingTsExtensions, the new module must not import any ".ts" specifier — a NodeNext ".js" specifier (the convention already used throughout tools/packaging) is the only safe form.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD — REWRITE THE INTEGRATION TEST TO CONSUME THE CANONICAL INVENTORY, in tests/integration/distribution/distribution-packaging.test.ts.

Delete the test's own hand-built `INVENTORY` and import the canonical one from tools/packaging/distribution-inventory.ts instead. That removes the duplicate AUTHORITY task rail 1 forbids.

BUT KEEP THE PIN, and this is the step's whole risk. Once the test imports the array it asserts, any expectation DERIVED from that array compares it with itself and survives every future omission. So:
- keep `expect(INVENTORY.length).toBe(6)` with 6 as a LITERAL;
- keep the six component ids spelled out literally (control-room, daemon, ide-adapter-jetbrains, mcp-bridge, provider-claude, provider-codex — the set already at :369);
- keep the ten jetbrains asset paths spelled out literally, so a dropped or added asset reddens rather than silently redefining the shipped subject.
The canonical inventory is the SUBJECT of these assertions, never the source of them.

Add the DoD 3 failure cases, each asserting the EXACT existing stable reason code and its owning layer — `COMPONENT_SET_INCOMPLETE` is already in use (:487), so reuse it rather than minting a code: omission of a component, duplication of one, asset drift within a component, and a caller-supplied alternative inventory.

These fail until step 3 lands.

LAND THE CANONICAL INVENTORY. Create `tools/packaging/distribution-inventory.ts` — one frozen production list naming exactly the six shipped components.

Carry each component's `componentId`, `componentKind` and exact `assets`, with ide-adapter-jetbrains and its ten real asset paths included. `DISTRIBUTION_COMPONENT_KINDS` already contains `IDE_ADAPTER` (test :242), so the kind vocabulary needs no extension.

HAND-WRITTEN AND FROZEN, NOT GENERATED. Do not derive the asset lists from a directory walk: they are the subject of a distribution digest, and deriving them would make the shipped subject depend on whatever is on disk at build time — exactly what a canonical inventory exists to prevent.

Paths stay FORWARD-SLASH LOGICAL PATHS, never OS-joined. `readOwned` (release-subject.mjs:102-103) splits on "/" and calls `resolve`, and this repo ships on Windows.

Freeze the array and each entry, matching the existing `Object.freeze` discipline in release-subject.mjs:45-51.

Keep the module under 250 lines (task rail 3) — six components with explicit asset lists should land near 150.

Run the step-2 tests; they must now pass.

MAKE THE RELEASE SUBJECT CONSUME IT (DoD 2), in scripts/release/release-subject.mjs.

Replace the five-entry `RELEASE_COMPONENTS` literal (:45-51) with an import of the canonical inventory, using an explicit `.ts` extension — step 1's probe proved node v24.16.0 resolves that from a `.mjs` with no build step. Keep the exported name `RELEASE_COMPONENTS` if anything else imports it; check before renaming.

`buildReleaseSubject`'s accepted subject must now bind all SIX component manifests/container digests to the same exact source SHA and distribution contract. The sixth component flows through the existing machinery — do not add a special case for jetbrains.

DO NOT WEAKEN `readComponents` (:96-99). Its `JSON.stringify(value) === JSON.stringify(RELEASE_COMPONENTS)` comparison is order-sensitive BY DESIGN and is the whole of DoD 3's caller-supplied-alternative refusal. It must now refuse against the six-entry canonical list. Resist replacing it with a set or length comparison to accommodate the new entry — that would silently accept a reordered or substituted inventory. Leave the empty-array early return at :98 exactly as it is; it is out of scope even if it looks odd.

PRESERVE distribution signature, parser, verifier, compatibility and source-binding authority (task rail 2). This task changes inventory COMPOSITION only.

PUT THE NEW MODULE UNDER THE PACKAGING TYPECHECK — a FOURTH owned path beyond the task's stated three, named deliberately rather than smuggled in.

`typecheck:packaging` (package.json:27) is an explicit file list naming only distribution-build.ts and distribution-startup.ts, with no glob. Add `tools/packaging/distribution-inventory.ts` to it.

WHY THIS IS NOT OPTIONAL: DoD 5's verification is `pnpm typecheck:packaging && pnpm test:integration`. Without this edit that command still exits 0 while the new production module is never typechecked — the gate reports success for a file it did not look at, the same invisible-to-the-gate failure as a missing `.js` bridge. Note the command's strict flags (`--strict --exactOptionalPropertyTypes --noUncheckedIndexedAccess --verbatimModuleSyntax`); the new module must satisfy all of them, and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` in particular affects how frozen arrays are indexed.

Change NOTHING else in package.json. If the scope expansion is unacceptable to review, the alternative is to report blocked rather than leave the module untypechecked — do not silently accept a vacuous gate.

Run `pnpm typecheck:packaging` and confirm it now compiles three files and exits 0.

MUTATION DRILLS. Capture `sha256sum` of each target BEFORE mutating; restore by Edit and verify by `sha256sum` against the captured hash. Never `git checkout` — it reverts to HEAD and would destroy this task's untracked new module, and `git diff` is blind to untracked files so an empty diff proves nothing.

D1 — OMISSION. Remove ide-adapter-jetbrains from the canonical inventory. A NAMED test must go red on the literal count and on the component-id assertion. If only the count reddens, the ids are not pinned; if neither does, the test is deriving its expectation from the array under test and is vacuous — fix the test, not the drill.

D2 — ASSET DRIFT. Remove ONE of the ten jetbrains asset paths. A NAMED test must redden on the exact-asset-set assertion. This is the drill that proves the shipped subject cannot change silently, which is the point of the whole task.

D3 — DUPLICATION. Add a second entry with an existing componentId. A NAMED test must redden with the exact stable reason code and its owning layer.

D4 — CALLER-SUPPLIED ALTERNATIVE. Weaken `readComponents` (:96-99) from the byte comparison to a length check. A NAMED test must redden — proving the guard still refuses a substituted or reordered inventory rather than merely one of the wrong size.

D5 — THE TYPECHECK LIST. Remove distribution-inventory.ts from `typecheck:packaging` and introduce a deliberate type error in it. `pnpm typecheck:packaging` must still EXIT 0 — demonstrating the gap step 5 closed. Restore both.

For each drill record the test name and the assertion that reddened.

GATE, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, COMMIT (DoD 5). Each leg's exit code read SEPARATELY — a `&&`-chained run reports one status for both legs:
1. `pnpm typecheck:packaging; echo "PACKAGING_EXIT=$?"`
2. `pnpm test:integration; echo "INTEGRATION_EXIT=$?"`
Both must print 0. Record the vitest summary line and confirm a NONZERO executed test count. Note `test:integration` itself begins with `pnpm typecheck:packaging` and ends with `node --test tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs`, so the plain-Node path IS exercised — that run is DoD 4's loadability evidence, not a separate claim.

`grep -c ''` tools/packaging/distribution-inventory.ts: under 250.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW — invoke the skill, then check what is specific here:
1. Does any test assertion derive its expectation from the imported inventory? That is the array policing itself. The six ids, the literal 6, and the ten asset paths must all be hand-written.
2. Is there any second inventory left anywhere — in the release script, the integration test, or a helper?
3. Does `readComponents` still do a byte comparison, and does it still refuse a reordered list?
4. Did the distribution signature, parser, verifier, compatibility or source-binding authority change? All are out of scope.
5. Are the inventory's paths forward-slash logical paths, not OS-joined?
6. Is distribution-inventory.ts actually in the typecheck:packaging list? D5 is the evidence.
7. Any probe or scratch file left behind? Epic rail 5 — the step-1 import probe must be long gone.

COMMIT BY EXPLICIT PATHSPEC naming the four owned paths: tools/packaging/distribution-inventory.ts, scripts/release/release-subject.mjs, tests/integration/distribution/distribution-packaging.test.ts, package.json. Never `git add -A` (epic rail 3).

HANDOFF: record task-01c5f96ec1e247dc846fd628c929974a as the real evidence consumer (DoD 4), and state plainly that package.json was a fourth owned path beyond the three the task named, with the reason — otherwise the extra file reads to QA as scope creep rather than a closed gate gap.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
THE SUBTLETY THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS TASK IS WORTH ANYTHING. Task rail 1 says "both production release and tests consume the one canonical inventory", and DoD 1 forbids "duplicate inventory authority in the release script or integration test". Read naively, that turns the integration test's `expect(INVENTORY.length).toBe(6)` into a check of the imported array against itself — a table policing its own generator, which passes forever and proves nothing.

The resolution is a distinction the plan states explicitly:
- DUPLICATE AUTHORITY is a second list that something CONSUMES as truth. That is what must go — today the test builds its own six-entry INVENTORY and the release script has a different five-entry one.
- A TEST PIN is literal expected values the test asserts the canonical inventory EQUALS. That must stay, and is the only thing keeping the test honest.
So the test imports the canonical inventory as its SUBJECT and asserts it against hand-written literals: the six component ids spelled out, the count as a literal 6, and the exact jetbrains asset paths spelled out. One authority, one real pin.

TWO CONSTRAINTS THE DESCRIPTION DOES NOT MENTION, both measured:

1. `pnpm typecheck:packaging` IS AN EXPLICIT FILE LIST, NOT A GLOB (package.json:27 names `tools/packaging/distribution-build.ts tools/packaging/distribution-startup.ts`). A new module under tools/packaging is therefore NOT typechecked unless it is added to that command. DoD 5 requires `pnpm typecheck:packaging` to exit 0 — which it would do vacuously while the new production module went unchecked. This is the same failure class as a missing `.js` bridge: invisible to the gate that is supposed to catch it. The fix requires editing package.json, which is NOT in the task's three stated owned paths, so the plan names it as a fourth owned path and flags the scope expansion rather than planning around it.

2. THE `.mjs` -> `.ts` IMPORT WORKS, verified by probe rather than assumed. `release-subject.mjs` is plain ESM with JSDoc types and must import a `.ts` module. Probe on node v24.16.0: a `.mjs` importing `./x.ts` with the explicit extension printed its value and exited 0 (probe deleted in the same command). So DoD 4's "loads under plain Node 24" is achievable with a direct `.ts` specifier and no build step. Had this failed, the whole shape would have needed a different answer.

REJECTED: generating the inventory from the filesystem. The asset lists are the SUBJECT of a distribution digest; deriving them from a directory walk would make the shipped subject depend on whatever happens to be on disk at build time, which is precisely what a canonical inventory exists to prevent. Hand-written and frozen is correct here.

planningNotes.risks:
THE TEST CAN GO VACUOUS IN THE ACT OF FIXING IT. Once the integration test imports the canonical inventory, `expect(INVENTORY.length).toBe(6)` is only meaningful because 6 is a hand-written literal. If any assertion derives its expectation from the imported array — counting it, mapping its ids and comparing to itself — the test compares the array with itself and survives every future omission. Keep the six ids and the ten jetbrains asset paths spelled out LITERALLY in the test; the canonical inventory is the SUBJECT, never the source of the expectation.

THE NEW MODULE IS UNTYPECHECKED BY DEFAULT. `typecheck:packaging` is an explicit two-file list (package.json:27). Adding distribution-inventory.ts without adding it there leaves it unchecked while the gate still exits 0 — the same invisible-to-the-gate failure as a missing `.js` bridge. package.json is a FOURTH owned path beyond the task's stated three; that expansion is deliberate and disclosed, not incidental.

DO NOT WEAKEN `readComponents`. Its byte comparison at :96-99 is order-sensitive by design and is the whole of DoD 3's caller-supplied-alternative refusal. Swapping it for a set comparison or a length check to accommodate the sixth entry would silently accept a reordered or substituted inventory. Also note the empty-array early return at :98 returns the empty list rather than refusing — confirm whether that is intended before changing anything around it, and do not "fix" it as a side effect of this task.

ASSET DRIFT IS THE POINT, NOT A DETAIL. The jetbrains component ships ten exact paths including `.js`/`.ts` pairs. If the canonical list drops or adds one, the distribution digest changes silently. The drift test must assert the exact set, and the mutation drill must prove a single removed asset reddens a named test.

DO NOT GENERATE THE INVENTORY FROM THE FILESYSTEM. These asset lists are the subject of a distribution digest; deriving them from a directory walk makes the shipped subject depend on whatever is on disk at build time.

PRESERVE EVERYTHING ELSE (task rail 2): distribution signature, parser, verifier, compatibility and source-binding authority are untouched. This task changes subject inventory COMPOSITION only.

CROSS-PLATFORM: `readOwned` (release-subject.mjs:102-103) resolves logical paths by splitting on "/" and calling `resolve`, so the inventory's paths must stay forward-slash logical paths, never OS-joined. This repo ships on Windows and the integration lane already has a drive-letter hazard with MSYS tooling.

CONSUMER (DoD 4): task-01c5f96ec1e247dc846fd628c929974a is the real evidence consumer and must be recorded, not merely mentioned.
